about: Water bases and additives for water recipes (catalog/water/). gh = general hardness and kh = alkalinity, both in ppm as CaCO₃, added by `ref.amount` of `ref.unit` in `ref.volume` of water. null = not published (shown as unknown, never guessed). Salts are calculated from molar mass; products cite the maker or a published source.

bases.name: Distilled
bases.note: No minerals: the usual starting point for recipes.

bases.name: Reverse osmosis (RO)
bases.note: Close to zero but varies by system: measure yours and enter it.

bases.name: ZeroWater (filtered)
bases.note: Treated as zero while the filter's meter reads 000; replace the filter when it doesn't.

bases.name: Tap
bases.note: Varies by place and season: check your water report or test it, and enter the numbers.

bases.name: Bottled spring water
bases.note: Enter the hardness and alkalinity from the label or your test.

additives.name: Epsom salt (magnesium sulfate)
additives.note: Calculated from the molar mass of MgSO₄·7H₂O (246.47 g/mol): ppm as CaCO₃ from 1 g in 1 L.

additives.name: Calcium chloride (dihydrate)
additives.note: Calculated from the molar mass of CaCl₂·2H₂O (147.01 g/mol): ppm as CaCO₃ from 1 g in 1 L.

additives.name: Calcium chloride (anhydrous)
additives.note: Calculated from the molar mass of CaCl₂ (110.98 g/mol): ppm as CaCO₃ from 1 g in 1 L. Check your package: most food-grade calcium chloride is the dihydrate.

additives.name: Magnesium chloride (hexahydrate)
additives.note: Calculated from the molar mass of MgCl₂·6H₂O (203.30 g/mol): ppm as CaCO₃ from 1 g in 1 L.

additives.name: Baking soda (sodium bicarbonate)
additives.note: Calculated from the molar mass of NaHCO₃ (84.007 g/mol): ppm as CaCO₃ from 1 g in 1 L.

additives.name: Potassium bicarbonate
additives.note: Calculated from the molar mass of KHCO₃ (100.115 g/mol): ppm as CaCO₃ from 1 g in 1 L.

additives.name: Lotus Calcium
additives.note: One drop in 450 ml adds 10 ppm hardness (as CaCO₃).

additives.name: Lotus Magnesium
additives.note: One drop in 450 ml adds 10 ppm hardness (as CaCO₃).

additives.name: Lotus Sodium (bicarbonate)
additives.note: One drop in 450 ml adds 5 ppm alkalinity (as CaCO₃).

additives.name: Lotus Potassium (bicarbonate)
additives.note: One drop in 450 ml adds 5 ppm alkalinity (as CaCO₃).

additives.name: Third Wave Water Classic Light Roast
additives.note: One stick per gallon: TDS 150 mg/L, alkalinity 36–40 mg/L (citrate buffering). Third Wave Water doesn't publish the hardness.

additives.name: Third Wave Water Medium Roast
additives.note: One stick per gallon: TDS ~150 mg/L, alkalinity ~80 mg/L. Third Wave Water doesn't publish the hardness.

additives.name: Third Wave Water Dark Roast
additives.note: One stick per gallon: TDS ~180 mg/L, alkalinity ~135–140 mg/L. Third Wave Water doesn't publish the hardness.

additives.name: Third Wave Water Espresso Machine
additives.note: One stick per gallon: TDS ~150 mg/L, alkalinity ~80 mg/L. Third Wave Water doesn't publish the hardness.

additives.name: Third Wave Water Cold Brew
additives.note: Magnesium sulfate, sodium and potassium bicarbonate. Third Wave Water doesn't publish its hardness or alkalinity.

additives.name: Barista Hustle Buffer concentrate
additives.note: Make it: 1.68 g baking soda dissolved in 1 L deionised water (about 1000 ppm KH). Calculated from the baking soda's molar mass: 1 g of it in 1 L of finished water adds about 1 ppm KH.

additives.name: Barista Hustle Hardness concentrate
additives.note: Make it: 2.45 g Epsom salt dissolved in 1 L deionised water (about 1000 ppm GH). Calculated from the Epsom salt's molar mass: 1 g of it in 1 L of finished water adds about 1 ppm GH.

additives.name: Barista Hustle original concentrate
additives.note: Make it: 8.6 g baking soda and 25 g Epsom salt in 500 g deionised water. Calculated from the salts' molar masses: 1 g of it in 1 L of finished water adds about 19 ppm GH and 9.6 ppm KH.

additives.name: Barista Hustle espresso concentrate
additives.note: Make it: 12.9 g baking soda and 25 g Epsom salt in 500 g deionised water. Calculated from the salts' molar masses: 1 g of it in 1 L of finished water adds about 18.9 ppm GH and 14.3 ppm KH.
